regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality test is whether it survives decomposition. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) looks solid, but manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 from 53.5 — the services sector is carrying the composite, and services PMI at 54.5 is itself a function of urban affluent spending that fuel inflation at 22.93% will erode within two quarters. IIP at 6.7% YoY, down from 8.8%, confirms the deceleration is already in the activity data, not just the forecast. The inversion worth making: RBI's own GDP forecast of 6.7% sits 110bps below the headline print — the statistical gap between GDP and GVA is doing work that genuine output growth is not.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is above the 4% midpoint target, but the composition is what should unsettle the RBI. Fuel inflation at 22.93% — a 95th-percentile print, up from 20.05% — is feeding directly into WPI at 9.92%, which means producer margins are being squeezed before the consumer even feels the full pass-through. Core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) appears benign, but that divergence between a low core and a spiking fuel component is precisely the setup where second-order effects — transport costs into food prices, logistics repricing — push headline CPI through 5% within two quarters. RBI's own inflation forecast has already moved to 5.1% from 4.6% — the committee is telling you what it sees.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — is the structural fault line. CD ratio at 81.4% has eased one month from 82.5% but remains at the 75th percentile historically; the last time India sustained above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14, and that episode ended with emergency macro-prudential tightening. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding channels are absorbing what retail deposit mobilisation cannot supply — a fragile bridge. Industry credit at 20% YoY and services at 22.9% suggest the demand for credit is genuine, which makes the funding mismatch more dangerous, not less.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% (38th percentile) with CPI at 4.45% and fuel inflation at 22.93% leaves the real rate at approximately 80bps — thin cover for a central bank watching its own inflation forecast rise 50bps in a single revision cycle. RBI is on hold, but the direction of the next move is being quietly repriced: with US 10Y at 4.97% and INR at a 91st-percentile 96.15, any rate cut would accelerate capital outflows and widen the current account. Housing affordability index at 3.5 (19th percentile) signals that the existing rate level is already compressing real estate demand — a cut would help affordability but arrive too late to prevent the inventory build already underway.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up from 75.6%, now at the 74th percentile — is the number that matters most for private capex timing. Historically, sustained utilisation above 75% is the threshold at which private sector balance sheets begin committing to greenfield investment; India crossed that threshold this month. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY confirms the commitment is translating into orders. The inversion: core sector growth at 5.4%, down from 6.0%, suggests the upstream inputs — steel, cement, electricity — are not yet accelerating to match the capex signal. Either the capex cycle is front-loaded on imports and equipment, or the IIP capital goods number is capturing order books rather than actual installation.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a strong print, but at a 71st-percentile reading it is not the record it appears — and the YTD GST at a 14th-percentile ₹10.43 lakh crore suggests the monthly spike is partly seasonal and partly advance filing. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% are the more honest consumption signal: two-wheeler growth at the 55th percentile indicates rural and semi-urban demand is recovering, not just the affluent urban segment. The tension: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (26th percentile, down from 5.6%) while vehicle loans grow at 18.8% — consumers are financing durables but pulling back on revolving credit, a pattern consistent with fuel-cost pressure on discretionary cash flow.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding stress as banks tighten retail deposit competition.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they will poach deposits from smaller peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; margin compression and refinancing risk are acute. RBI will likely signal liquidity support (OMOs, CRR cuts) within 6-8 weeks to prevent credit rationing. Position for rate cuts in H2 2026.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI easing or a sharp slowdown in credit growth. The last time this divergence was this wide (2022), it resolved via a 200bps rate cut cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks Into Capex Zone","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month). This is the 74th percentile historically and signals firms are bumping against constraints. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0%) but this deceleration is demand-driven, not supply-driven — a classic pre-capex signal.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks. Private capex orders should accelerate in Q1 FY27. Infrastructure plays (Nifty Infra) will outperform as government capex remains steady. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex-led growth crowds out consumption.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest in 18 months. Historically, when CU exceeds 76%, capex announcements follow within 2-3 quarters. This is a lagging indicator of demand strength, not a leading one.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Surge Signals Affluent Money Entry","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (Mar 2026, up from ₹31,961 Cr prior month) — rising for two consecutive months. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (up from ₹18.21 Tr), growing at 93rd percentile. Critically: SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (up from 99.06 Cr) but SIP AUM growing 40% faster than account growth — average ticket size rising sharply. MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile), DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, rising two months in a row).","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour. Affluent retail (HNI/UHNI) is entering via SIPs, not mass retail. Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks and quality midcaps. Avoid micro-cap and speculative plays — they will underperform when this cohort rotates. Equity MF net inflows will sustain, but expect volatility as foreign flows remain choppy (FII at ₹29,631 Cr, up from -₹3,111 Cr but still fragile).","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile is a 10-year high. When SIP ticket size rises this sharply, it historically precedes a 6-12 month period of steady but decelerating equity inflows, followed by a correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month) — 95th percentile, the highest in 18 months. Brent crude at $108.41/bbl (75th percentile, up from $95.30 five months ago). WTI at $105.42/bbl (86th percentile). This is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78%), which is at 67th percentile. Food inflation at 5.52% YoY (up from 5.32%), adding to headline CPI pressure.","implication":"Margin compression is imminent for refiners, logistics, and transport-heavy sectors (airlines, e-commerce, FMCG). Overweight energy stocks (oil majors, refiners) and underweight consumer discretionary. RBI will struggle to cut rates if fuel inflation persists — expect a 50bps cut in June, then a pause. Hedge currency exposure; INR weakness (96.15 vs 95.84) will amplify import costs.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically preceded a 200-300bps spike in headline CPI within 2-3 months. The last time this occurred (2022), it forced RBI to hike rates aggressively.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Sticky, BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 4.97% (90th percentile, up from 4.73% five months ago) — rising for four of last five months. Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile) — tightening cycle underway. US core CPI at 2.45% (falling two months in a row, 47th percentile), but Fed is data-dependent and unlikely to cut before June. DXY at 99.61 (flat, 48th percentile) but sticky above 99.","implication":"Carry trades are unwinding. JPY strength will pressure EM currencies, including INR. FII flows to India will remain volatile — expect outflows if US yields stay >4.8%. Overweight USD-denominated assets and underweight EM equities. RBI will need to defend INR via intervention (reserves are adequate at ~$600bn), but this will constrain rate cuts. Position for a 50bps cut in June, then a pause through H2 2026.","pct_10y":90,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 90th percentile is the highest since 2023. When US rates are this elevated and sticky, EM central banks typically cut rates to defend currencies, creating a policy divergence that pressures equity valuations.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates, RBI Intervention Looms","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.84 prior month, 91st percentile) — rising for three of last five months. This is the weakest level in 18 months. FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (up from -₹3,111 Cr, but volatile). US 10Y at 4.97% (90th percentile) is pulling capital away from India. India VIX at 13.43 (up from 12.29%, 8th percentile) — volatility is rising, signalling outflow risk.","implication":"RBI will intervene to defend 96.50 as a hard floor. Expect RBI to sell dollars from reserves (currently adequate but declining). This will constrain liquidity and may force a pause in rate cuts. Overweight INR hedges (long USD forwards, short INR calls). Avoid FII-dependent sectors (IT, pharma); domestic-focused sectors (banks, FMCG, utilities) will outperform. Monitor FII flows weekly — a sustained outflow >₹5,000 Cr/week will trigger RBI action.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness is a 10-year high. Historically, when INR breaks 96, RBI intervenes aggressively, and rate cuts are delayed by 2-3 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decouples From IT Stock Proxy","data_text":"Office absorption at 26.9 mn sqft (up from 24.1 mn sqft, 21st percentile — historically weak). Nifty IT index flat YoY while office rents in Bengaluru at ₹102/sqft (up from ₹94.4, 58th percentile) and Mumbai at ₹125/sqft (up from ₹121, 38th percentile). Office vacancy at 14.5% (down from 16.1%, 42nd percentile). Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (down from 11.6%, 35th percentile). Home loan disbursements at ₹25,900 Cr (up from ₹228 Cr, but data is volatile). Affordability index at 3.5 (down from 0.48, 19th percentile — housing is becoming unaffordable).","implication":"GCCs (Global Capability Centers) and non-IT corporates are the real office buyers, not traditional IT services. This means IT services companies are NOT the proxy for commercial real estate strength. Overweight commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) and underweight Nifty IT. Housing affordability is collapsing — avoid residential RE plays; focus on commercial and logistics. The office market is bifurcating: prime locations (Bengaluru, Mumbai) are tight, but secondary markets are soft. This is a structural shift away from IT-centric demand.","pct_10y":21,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 21st percentile is weak, yet rents are rising — this signals supply constraints in prime locations, not demand strength. Historically, when absorption is weak but rents rise, it precedes a supply glut in 12-18 months as developers rush to build.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 6.7% RBI forecast sitting 110bps below it is not a confidence interval — it is a warning about statistical construction. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) flatters: manufacturing slipped to 52.8 while services held at 54.5, meaning the composite is a weighted average of a decelerating goods economy and a still-buoyant services sector that fuel at 22.93% inflation will begin to tax within two quarters. IIP at 6.7% YoY — down from 8.8% — confirms momentum is already fading in the activity data. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the one unambiguously positive signal: private capex commitments follow this number with a 2-3 quarter lag, and the threshold has been crossed.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y at 4.97% — rising four of the last five months to a 90th-percentile yield — is the gravitational constant around which every other asset is now orbiting. US GDP at 1.5% SAAR (down from 2.1%) with core CPI falling to 2.45% creates the paradox: the economy is slowing, yet the Fed cannot cut because US headline CPI at 3.35% is rising and the BOJ's rate hike to 1.0% is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded global risk appetite. Euro Stoxx 50 at a 100th-percentile 6,237 — sliding five consecutive sessions — while China GDP decelerates to 4.3% (from 5.0%) and China PMI composite at 49.5 signals contraction: the synchronised global recovery priced into equities is not showing up in the activity data.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore — a 100th-percentile print, rising two consecutive months — is the single largest domestic absorption event on record, and it is doing the work that FII equity net at ₹29,631 crore (volatile, up from -₹3,112 crore prior month) cannot be relied upon to sustain. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh crore (93rd percentile) growing 40% faster than SIP account additions signals rising average ticket size — affluent savers are increasing allocation, not new retail participants entering. The structural risk: bank credit at 17.1% against deposit growth of 10.8% means the banking system is funding credit expansion through wholesale markets and NBFC channels — a 630bps divergence that tightens the moment global risk appetite turns.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 55,795 — down from 57,381 five sessions ago, at a 92nd-percentile level — is the index most exposed to the CD ratio fault line: NIM compression from deposit rate competition, macro-prudential risk weight tightening on unsecured lending, and NBFC funding stress are three separate vectors pointing at the same earnings outcome. Nifty 50 at 23,119 (74th percentile, down five of six sessions) with India VIX rising to 13.43 from a 5th-percentile 10.68 three weeks ago signals that the complacency trade is unwinding — slowly, but the direction is set. Office REITs — Embassy at ₹369.92, Mindspace at ₹345.06, Brookfield at ₹263.49 — are all down 15-30% from prior levels despite office absorption rising to 26.9 mn sqft; the REIT derating is a rate story, not a demand story, and it will not reverse until US 10Y peaks.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact. First: fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) with Brent at $108.41/bbl — every $10 adds approximately $15bn to India's import bill, widening CAD by 40bps and pushing INR through 97 — forces RBI to hold or tighten precisely when growth is decelerating, a policy trap with no clean exit. Second: CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY — if wholesale funding costs rise 50bps in response to US 10Y at 4.97%, the NBFC segment faces a margin-and-liquidity squeeze simultaneously, the same sequence that preceded the IL&FS stress of 2018. Third: China GDP at 4.3% with PMI composite at 49.5 — a contraction signal — threatens copper at $6.46/lb (76th percentile) and iron ore at $161.91, which would compress India's metals and mining earnings even as domestic capex is accelerating. Watch Friday's US core PCE print at 3.34% — if it rises, the Fed's June cut consensus dissolves and the INR-Brent-CAD chain tightens further.

"}
